correctness.rationale: PASS: For an isotropic strongly convex quadratic on closed convex X, constrained first-order stationarity and the radius inequality 2<x−x*,y−x*> >= ||y−x*||² imply E=<∇f(x),y−x*> >= μ||y−x*||²/2. Hence the exact local linear minimizer is uniquely x* and the absolute-gap factor 2 is sharp at X=R², x=(1,1), y=(2,0). In one dimension order yields E/Δ=||y−x*||/R. For d>=2 triangle inequality gives at most 2, and the halfspace X={z2>=0}, x=(1,a), y=(2,0), c=(0,C) with C≥(2/η−1−a²)/a gives E=2, Δ≥2/η and ratio 2/sqrt(1+a²)→2. Exact rational checks at η=1/10,1/2,1 gave Δ=20,4,2 and ratio near 2 at a=1/1000. Applies to one-step ideal radius only; upper value 2 is supremum, not asserted attained.
